title: Contrast-driven fidelity sweep for microbatch + TTL interplay
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: quantify end-to-end tradeoffs between tail latency and generation quality when changing two orthogonal runtime knobs: microbatch size and prefix/kv cache TTL. This ticket drives an eval suite and canary criteria that tie measured quality regressions to specific config deltas so we can safely roll batching/cache tuning patches without surprising customers.

Motivation: previous config tweaks reduced p50 latency but occasionally regressed n-gram overlap and semantic metrics for particular short-dialog slices. We need an automated, slice-aware contrast evaluation that associates quality deltas with configuration axes and supports canary thresholds for rollout/rollback.

Scope: build a sweep harness that runs cross-product configs for microbatch {1,2,4,8} x cache_ttl_seconds {0,30,120,600} across representative workloads (short Q&A, multi-turn chat, instruction-following). Produce per-slice latency distributions, utility metrics (ROUGE-L, BLEU-lite, BERTScore), and business-facing metrics (latency p50/p95/p99, token cost delta). Define statistical tests and practical thresholds for triggering an automatic rollback or conservative traffic weighting in canaries.
acceptance_criteria: Sweep harness can run cross-product configs and persist results to experiment store
Per-slice dashboards created showing latency distribution and quality metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, BERTScore, SemanticEM)
Statistical test defined (bootstrap + effect size) and implemented to detect regressions at slice-level with configurable alpha
Canary gating rules expressed as JSON policy and validated against historical baseline with no false-positive rollbacks in 30-day replay
PR with harness and dashboard wiring merged and e2e smoke tests passing in CI
test_plan: 1) Run baseline (current default config) against eval corpus and persist metrics
2) For each config in the cross-product, run 3 repeats seeded differently and collect p50/p95/p99 latency, token-cost, and quality metrics
3) Compute per-slice delta vs baseline and perform bootstrap confidence intervals + Cliff's delta for effect size
4) Flag slices with high effect size and >X absolute quality drop or >Y% latency improvement for reviewer attention
5) Replay the canary policy on 30 days of production trace (sampled requests) to validate no spurious rollbacks
6) Run scale smoke on a staging Dedicated pool to ensure load patterns don't alter behavior
datasets_and_slices: core-eval-2026-v2 (10k examples): short-QA (<=32 tokens), multi-turn-chat (2-6 turns), instruction (longer completions)
customer-pattern-sample-2026 (sanitized) - high-frequency prompts from onboarding bucket
adversarial-slice: short prompts with high lexical overlap (sensitive to caching)
analysis_and_decision_criteria: We will consider a config change unsafe if any slice shows: (a) a statistically significant quality drop (bootstrap CI excludes 0 at alpha=0.01) AND effect size (Cliff's delta) >= 0.33, OR (b) a >5% absolute drop in business metric semantic_em for slices marked high-priority. Conversely, latency wins must provide >=10% reduction in p95 with <1% increase in token-cost. Canary gating policy will encode these rules and allow manual override with documented justification.

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Synthetic evals may not surface rare customer-facing regressions. Mitigation: include sampled production traces in replay and require canary validation on real traffic sample before 100% rollout.
Risk: Statistical false positives due to multiple comparisons across slices. Mitigation: apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control and require effect size threshold in addition to p-value.
Risk: Experiment runtime cost. Mitigation: schedule heavy sweeps on off-peak Dedicated pool and optionally downsample repeats after initial signal detection.
follow_up: After first full sweep, schedule a cross-functional review (PM/Design/Eng/SRE) to agree on canary thresholds. If a risky slice is identified, create follow-up tickets to instrument additional telemetry and attempt localized mitigations (e.g., cache warm policies, tokenization alignment).
